original_question: For isotropic composites made from two isotropic elastic phases, with one phase possibly rigid or void, can one derive bounds on the achievable effective bulk and shear modulus pairs (kappa*,mu*) that improve on the current best-known inequalities, and ultimately determine the optimal bounds exactly?
target_in_paper: Section 4, Problem 4.7 (p. 14): "Can one obtain improved bounds on the elastic moduli pairs of isotropic composites of two isotropic elastic phases, and ultimately find the optimal ones?" The immediately preceding context adds that one phase may be rigid or void and that the tightest known pair-bounds are those of Cherkaev-Gibiansky in 2D and Berryman-Milton in 3D. ([par.nsf.gov](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10232880))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right mathematical object—the attainable effective bulk/shear modulus pairs (κ*, μ*)—the right material class—two-phase isotropic elastic composites with nearby rigid/void special-case motivation—and the right research aim: improve the best available inequalities and ultimately determine the optimal bounds. This is substantively very close to Problem 4.7. ([par.nsf.gov](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10232880))
missing_details: The paper’s official target is the broader Section 4, Problem 4.7, not the narrower void-only questions in Problems 4.2–4.4; the rigid/void wording comes from the surrounding context and from Problem 4.1. ([par.nsf.gov](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10232880))

To be fully stand-alone, the question should specify that the spatial dimension is two or three, since the paper distinguishes the known 2D bounds from the known 3D bounds. ([par.nsf.gov](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10232880))

The fixed input data should be named: the two phase bulk/shear moduli and the prescribed phase volume fractions, because the attainable (κ*, μ*) region depends on these parameters; Section 4 frames the elasticity G-closure in terms of two isotropic phases in prescribed volume fractions. ([par.nsf.gov](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10232880))

‘Isotropic composites’ should be unpacked as composites whose homogenized effective elasticity tensor is isotropic, so that it is completely described by the pair (κ*, μ*). ([par.nsf.gov](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10232880))

‘Current best-known inequalities’ should be identified explicitly as the Cherkaev-Gibiansky bounds in two dimensions and the Berryman-Milton bounds in three dimensions. ([par.nsf.gov](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10232880))

If one wishes to retain the rigid/void language from the draft, it should be presented as an allowed limiting/special case inside the broader two-isotropic-phase problem, not as a restriction of the official statement. ([par.nsf.gov](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10232880))

Not applicable here: this is a continuum-elasticity/G-closure question, so there are no ambient ring/field, homogeneity-degree, nilpotency, operator-power, or ‘for all sufficiently large m’ clauses to specify. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.03394))
refined_question: Fix d ∈ {2,3}, two isotropic elastic phases with bulk and shear moduli (κ1, μ1) and (κ2, μ2), and prescribed phase volume fractions, allowing the limiting special cases in which one phase is rigid or void. Among all microgeometries whose homogenized effective elasticity tensor is isotropic, determine the sharp attainable set of effective bulk/shear pairs (κ*, μ*). In particular, can one improve the presently best pair-bounds—Cherkaev-Gibiansky in d = 2 and Berryman-Milton in d = 3—and ultimately determine the optimal bounds exactly?
justification: The draft is closest to Section 4, Problem 4.7, because that is the paper’s official open problem about improving and ultimately optimizing bounds on attainable effective modulus pairs for isotropic composites of two isotropic elastic phases. I did not center the rewrite on Problem 4.2, even though your mention of a rigid/void phase points toward that nearby discussion, because Problem 4.2 is the narrower void-special-case question about improving μ* - cκ* ≤ μ or approaching (0, μ). I also did not center it on Problem 4.6, because that concerns the more specialized subcase of three-dimensional isotropic elastic polycrystals rather than arbitrary two-phase isotropic composites. ([par.nsf.gov](https://par.nsf.gov/servlets/purl/10232880))
